quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: What can happen if you brake too hard?

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Coming to a complete stop before you expect to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause you to lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass if you can do so safely. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster.

questions.question: A motorcycle's front brake provides about how much of its total stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What should you do with a motorcycle helmet after a crash?
questions.explanation: Always replace any helmet that has been worn during a crash.

questions.question: Your tire goes flat while riding. How should you stop?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: Grip the handgrips firmly. Ease off the throttle and go straight. Gradually brake only on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: Is always the right portion of the lane.
Is always the center portion of the lane.
Is always the left portion of the lane.
Varies based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Varies based on road, weather, and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Change your position based on road conditions, weather, and traffic.

questions.question: Which is true when passing another vehicle?

options.text: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone if the pass was started before the no passing zone began.
You may exceed the speed limit.
You should pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow posted speed limits and only happen in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located on the left handgrip of a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Stay out of other drivers' blind spots.
Give you a good view of the shoulder.
Make it hard to see road hazards.
Encourage others to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of other drivers' blind spots.
questions.explanation: Choose your lane position so you can see others and they can see you. Do not ride in another driver's blind spot for a long time.

questions.question: When traveling on a motorcycle with a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Not on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: The passenger should ride in the sidecar. They must keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Keep your intentions hidden from other drivers.
Always stay within a foot of another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Stay visible to other drivers to reduce crash risk. Use your signals, brake lights, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Why should a load be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Other drivers cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load placed too high raises the motorcycle's center of gravity and makes it harder to keep the motorcycle balanced.

questions.question: When selecting a helmet, make sure it is all of the following, except:

options.text: Approved by the U.S. Department of Transportation.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fits snugly, and has no damage such as cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: If you can't avoid a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Speed up and lean the motorcycle.
Speed up and keep the motorcycle upright.
Slow down and lean the motorcycle.
Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and keep the motorcycle upright.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid a slippery surface, keep your motorcycle upright and go as slowly as possible.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Stopping is easier than without a sidecar.
Stopping takes longer than without a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same as without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping takes longer than without a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight and requires more braking force to stop. Slowing and stopping take longer downhill than on flat ground.

questions.question: When riding in fog, you should:

options.text: Switch between low and high beams.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use high beams when riding near other vehicles.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear too quickly, what could happen?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light may turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear too quickly, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Slow down before shifting into a lower gear.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists in a group avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A driver merging may not see both riders.
Light reflecting off both helmets can make it hard for riders to see.
Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to move and avoid hazards.
It is hard for riders on the left to exit a highway from a pair.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs does not give riders enough space to move and avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists in a group should not ride in pairs. Each rider needs enough space to maneuver and avoid hazards.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where should you get the main information about your motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual first. It has specific information about your motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: Which body part operates the gearshift lever?
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT necessary for an effective eye or face shield?
questions.explanation: An effective shield must be free of scratches, resist penetration, fasten securely, and allow air to pass through. It does not need to be airtight. It should also allow room for eyeglasses or sunglasses underneath.
